name: Magistral Small 2506
definition: Magistral Small 2506 is a dense reasoning instruction model developed by Mistral AI in the Magistral family. It has 24B parameters, supports 128K nominal · 40K recommended for quality of context, accepts Text and produces Text. Its primary role is step-by-step reasoning, mathematics, science, coding and multilingual problem solving.

key_topics: step-by-step reasoning, mathematics, science, coding and multilingual problem solving

details: Reasoning-tuned through supervised traces from Magistral Medium plus reinforcement learning
128K context in the model, with publisher recommendation to limit to ~40K because performance may degrade beyond that

training.summary: Magistral Small adds explicit long-form reasoning behavior to the Mistral Small 3.1 base. Mistral describes supervised fine-tuning from Magistral Medium reasoning traces followed by reinforcement learning.

license.legal_note: OpenWeightModels summary for technical comparison; not legal advice.

deployments.notes: Official model uses a vLLM-oriented inference path.
Mistral says it can fit one RTX 4090 or a 32GB RAM MacBook once quantized.

hardware.summary: Quantized local deployment is realistic for a 24B model, but long chain-of-thought outputs and large context windows increase KV cache and generation time. Mistral explicitly recommends a 40K maximum model length for quality even though the architecture exposes 128K.

limitations: The nominal 128K window is not the same as a recommended 128K operating point.
Reasoning traces can be long and expensive to serve.
Benchmark scores are sensitive to sampling parameters; Mistral recommends temperature 0.7 and top_p 0.95 for the published setup.
Text-only model; no native image input.
